label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment:
quick: Took the skis out for a hike to Healy pass. Around 2200-2300m HS was 22-30cm, crust down 15-18cm near base of snowpack provides some protection from sharks, but there's still plenty out there. Lower snowpack beginning to facet around the crusts. 

We found coverage was best in open trees on lee aspects, kept to easy turns on mellow slopes to avoid rocks, spotted a few small sz 1 cornice sli…

reports.title: Rockisle and Wawa conditions
reports.comment:
quick: Went for a tour around Sunshine's sidecountry. Found significant variability in conditions at treeline, we skied on polar aspects where snow was still dry, but still early season conditions out there. Lots of rocks to hit, conservative skiing a must. Not enough snow for ski travel below treeline.

Between 2200-2350m HS 30-40, drifting up to 45. Surface variable, 2-4mm surface hoar on shelte…

reports.title: Sunshine meadows
reports.comment:
quick: Skiing is okay, crust in photo is 2cm thick and pencil hardness.

Many south facing slopes for the day had variable HS between 20 cm and 45cm.

Very visible wind affect in unsheltered areas like rock isle and near sunshine landing.

Crust was present in many places where we walked.

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows
reports.comment:
quick: +2 in the parking lot, treeline temperatures were around -3C all day with strong south to southwest winds and thick cloud and light snow.  The midpack was pretty weak consisting mostly of facets. Even on south aspects the suncusts barely supporting a skier.

Around any rocks you would sink to the ground.  Found a few good turns on mellow slopes in the trees away from boulders and rocks.  Al…

reports.title: Reactive windslab on Wawa
reports.comment: quick: Went for a ski on the North side of Wawa ridge, found wind affect on E / NE aspects, HS 40-50, deeper in loaded areas. Triggered a size 1 wind slab from the toe of a small NE roll and remote triggered a second sz 1 slab on the same feature that did not move. Estimated crown depth 30-50cm, ~15-20m wide, running ~10m. Slab broke at shallow spot near rocks with a small stepdown noted, suspect …

reports.title: Sunshine area
reports.comment:
quick: 30-40cm depth throughout the open areas
Widespread surface hoar throughout the meadow 5-10mm
Significant settlement, whumpfing, over a large area of the main face, north east facing aspect of quartz, no movement, approx 2400m

reports.title: Sunshine - WaWa Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Good travel conditions out to WaWa Ridge and back today, thanks to a melt-freeze crust just above the ground that supports your skis while traveling.

Snowpack is 40-60 cm deep and has a couple of weak layers in the lower half which are producing avalanches at the ski hill. We were surprised to find surface hoar in our profile.

But the ski penetrative was ankle deep soft pow with no wind e…

reports.title: Bourgeau ice climbs
reports.comment: quick: Didn't climb, just skied by and took a few pictures. Left looks very thin, Right looks better but hard to tell from below.

reports.title: Newfie Bowl, sunshine meadows
reports.comment:
quick: The last 5cm of snow came in without much wind.  New 3 to 9mm surface hoar and some sun made for fast snow.  South aspects were supportive. Sheltered East and North the midpack was weaker and we hit a few rocks. Went up to the Sunshine landing but the snow was pretty shallow and had some whumpfing. Over all good skiing in broken skies with light winds.  

On east aspects at 2150m October cr…

reports.title: Newfie Bowl Profile
reports.comment: quick: Small tour around Newfie bowl and Sunshine landing, calm winds, s-1, minimal evidence of windloading, coverage has improved quite a bit with recent storm, good powder skiing, but still rocks to hit out there. Dug a profile on easterly aspect at treeline in Newfie bowl, no fractures on compression tests aside from breaks in the top 10cm of storm snow. Features beginning to fill in, but steep…

reports.title: Bourgeau Right
reports.comment: quick: The route is in typical thin condition, with some short sections of unprotectable ice on slab. The approach is particularly shrubby this year. At lower elevations, there isn’t enough snow to generate an avalanche, but from the top of pitch four onward, the ledges are accumulating knee to thigh-deep deposits of snow and sluff debris. I’m unsure how much snow is in the bowl above, but I’d be …

reports.title: Quartz Hill Walk
reports.comment: quick: Took a walk to Quartz Hill to poke around. Avg. 60cm HS at TL. Wind scouring beginning in the alpine with leeward N-NE aspects starting to appear wind loaded. Small cornice developments were visible on the ridges. No obvious snowpack instabilities at TL. We had some fun mellow turns on the NW aspect. A few sharks still lingering for sure though. We dug a profile on the NE aspect. / snowpack…

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Healy trail was in good condition. With only a few rocks.  Meadows had 50cm of snow which was mostly soft -4F facets. The October crust on the ground was still moist but not there around rocks/ boulders. While skinning we sank through the midpack but skied pretty good when you didn't hit any rocks.  Skiing below 2100m off trail not possible. Small to medium surface hoar found up to 2400m on…

reports.title: SSV Backcountry
reports.comment: quick: Spent the last 2 days touring around SSV Slackcountry.  Temps ranged from -13 in the am to -9 at 2pm.  Light to mod NW winds bringing moist air and convective flurries along the divide resulting in 4cm of very low density snow above last week's storm snow.  Skiing in Newfie bowl yesterday (thurs) was very good (20cm ski pen) and mostly supportive if you could avoid tagging rocks.  Wawa bowl…

reports.title: Bourgeau Right Avalanche
reports.comment:
quick: Two parties on the route today. See avalanche report. / avalanche: While rapping Bourgeau right today the gully on climbers right had a loose snow avalanche that contained a good deal of rocks. 
Day was cloudy and calm, but at about 1400h the winds picked up and about 1500h the avalanche occurred. Scary bit everyone is fine.
Ps. Getting to the base of the route was the crux of the day… solo…

reports.title: Quartz
reports.comment: quick: Beautiful day on Quartz. Found some good turns on a lee aspect, though plenty of wind affect near ridge crest and lower down. No signs of instability noted.

reports.title: Simpson Pass
reports.comment: quick: Mellow walk up to the top of Wawa via Simpson Pass. Snow quality was ok, easy travel. Snow pack faceting.

reports.title: Rock Isle Lake
reports.comment: quick: little tour out around Rock Isle, nice day overall with some results in my first pit of the season. Nothing incredibly surprising with the hazard so we kept to the mellow slopes around the lake. Thanks to Zak for helping through the pit process / snowpack: see attached pit profile. Seeing results on buried surface hoar 18 down with good propagation on the ECT. On steeper slopes definitely w…

reports.title: Quartz Ridge & Hill
reports.comment:
quick: We skied to Quartz Ridge and Hill Sat Dec 21. 

The meadows: nice powdery snow, ankle-to-midcalf ski pen. 
 
Quartz ridge: barely had any snow (20 cm max?), and whatever was there was very wind-affected. 

Quart hill: Given the considerable hazard, we ruled out skiing the NE face even before we got there. We dropped the skies at the base of the ridge to Quartz Hill. The ridge had decent amo…

reports.title: FTC
reports.comment: quick: Evidence of a cornice failure in the days prior. There are large overhanging cornices on the western side of the slope from cross loading that need to be avoided.

reports.title: Grizzly trees - SSV slack
reports.comment: quick: Good conditions in Grizzly trees - HS 95cm with ski pen of 10-15cm which was supportive, boot pen to ground. Series of wind slabs around 2400m and higher - with a few settlements along the base of Twin  Cairns which is often typical of the area. No other signs of instability noted.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Super fun day on Sunshine slack country. There was definitely lots of wind affect, the top of the ridge was maybe 5-10 cm of snow total. However, we rode the wind loaded side which was great and maybe about 70-80 cm of snow with 10 cm of powder on top. There was a wind slab which we could see if we dug down about 30 cm, but no sign of propagation from anything or any activity. Further looke…

reports.title: Wawa Walk in the Woods
reports.comment: quick: Powder in the meadow on the way up. No signs of instability but slight wind affected snow along the ridge and Lee side of the ridge with small pockets of deposits that hadn't consolidated into a slab. Cornice formation along the western edge of the ridge. Tested cornices on small slopes and cornice disintegrated into small pieces.

reports.title: Spray River Falls
reports.comment:
quick: Excellent conditions on SRF today. Every pitch was just stellar. What a way to end 2024.

The weather was calm and moderately cold today. Flurries in the afternoon. Zero sign of instabilities or avalanches. Approach was straight forward with little snow.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Nice powder laps on the slopes below Wawa Ridge.  No instabilities or signs of recent avalanches noted.  Left the skis behind for a short walk up to the summit block; postholing with deep snow.  Moderate trailbreaking when stepping off existing skin tracks.

reports.title: Healy Pass Area
reports.comment: quick: Decent to good ski conditions at Healy Pass today, with a few groups out and about. Overall the snowpack was shallower and weaker than I expected (around 70 to 90 cm at treeline) and unsupportive facets were encountered while skiing up and down. Over a few hours of trail breaking, whumphing was encountered only a few times though all on the immediate Lee of the monarch ramparts at approxima…

reports.title: Fun Turns Couloir.
reports.comment:
quick: Some fun wiggles found in a coulior off the back of a well known ski resort - I forget the name - found 10-15 of fist on top of a moderately supportive crust. Some pretty excellent skiing to be had before it gets tracked out.

Some pinballing could be seen off the surrounding hills and recent avalanche activity was observed on the northern aspects of the hills opposite. 

Clattered a couple…

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Went into the Healy pass area Jan 7 and 8. Jan. 7 below Healy peak at 2300m elevation HS - 90cm. On south facing 25-deg slope had no results on CT. 1 thin firmer (1f+) layer 75cm from base, otherwise all fist density faceted sugary snow. Jan. 8 on western side of Monarch Ramparts at 2000m elevation HS - 105cm. On east facing 30-deg slope had no results on CT. Same thin firm layer roughly th…

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: 75 cm of snow at tree line. ECT at tree line produced no result. 5 cm of powder on top, varying sizes of facets below. Large facets at bottom of snow pack. Observed little wind affect (experinced no wind slab, could see cornices on far away slopes). More warming than expected, snow falling of trees during sunny periods of the day. Beautiful alpine glow for the ski out!

reports.title: Parker Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Super windy, we stayed below 2190m for some open tree runs. Top was supportive crust and windswept. Below 2140m snow was variable with up to 15cm of wind transported snow on top of the crust. CT no results on 27° NE aspect, hs 60-90cm. Saw a party that went to the top of the ridge and they said snow was very variable with mostly icey conditions. Overall very windswept with ground showing on…

reports.title: Wawa Ridge Pit + Riding
reports.comment:
quick: Conditions on the ridge were quite minimal. The windward side of the ridge was pretty bare and hard pack. The lee side had small cornice formation and lots of wind loading directly below the ridge. 

We dug an ECT 10m down from the ridge just above a plateau. Approx 15/20°slope angle. E aspect 2430m elevation. 10cm of wind slab broke with no propagation on 3rd tap. Rest of the test had no m…

reports.title: Sunshine meadows
reports.comment: quick: Strong sunlight combined with air temps around -7C at around noon with little to no wind. -21C early morning. Dug single column (CT) on northern aspect, sudden collapse at 18 with a clean break on facet layer 40cm down. Snowpack measured at 125cm. Column was dug in a fairly mellow area. Quartz hill shoulder doesn't have great coverage up close.

reports.title: Skier accidental avalanche on Quartz Hill, Banff NP
reports.comment:
avalanche: Avalanche occurred on February 8, 2025. Reported that the first person was still on the slope as the second person started down. Unsure where the slope was triggered from. At least one person rode to the bottom of the debris but stayed on the surface. No injuries and the group was able to ski out on their own.

The avalanche appeared to involve a steep 48° roll at the top that was mostl…

reports.title: Goat's Eye profile
reports.comment: snowpack: No result on the compression test - the entire snowpack would progressively collapse and crumble with each hit.  It's a weak stack of sugar!

reports.title: Twin Cairns Avalanche
reports.comment:
incident: Ascended Twin Cairns. Strong eastward wind transport was observed, with cornices formed on leeward slopes.
A snowboarder initiated descent on a convex roll into the steep East face, triggering a wind slab failure. The crown appears to be visible in two sections, possibly indicating a step-down failure which propagated into a larger avalanche (sz 2). The snowboarder was caught, carried ov…

reports.title: Its a spicy meatball
reports.comment: quick: Went to dig a pit outside sunshine to see the reactivity of persistent layer and go for a mellow ski. Heard notable whumpfs in mellow treed terrain on the way up to our dig spot. Snow skied like hot pow on south/se slopes. Wind effect was evident in subalpine/ treeline exposed area(3-15 cms of 4f) Got results on test (see snowpack tab). Top 3-5 became moist by 2 pm on southerly slopes. Ligh…

reports.title: Healy Pass and Center peak
reports.comment:
quick: Camped out at Healy creek and did some exploring sticking to mellow terrain around the Pass and Center peak. 

Strong wind on Thursday significantly degraded ski quality in alpine and treeline. Widespread wind effect with 5-50cm ski penetration depending on whether upper slab is supportive, or whether skis break through to wallow in the facets below. Solar aspects developing a breakable sun…

reports.title: Twin Cairns NE
reports.comment:
quick: It was a bluebird day, perfect for exploring, with a focus on mellow terrain while SPAW is in effect for the BNF forecasting region.

The lack of wind on Sunday resulted in hot weather, reaching temperatures of -2°C, combined with intense solar radiation. Exposed snow on the northern approach to Twin Cairns was severely affected by both wind and sun, resulting in minimal penetration while s…

reports.title: Size 2,5 avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: No signs of avalanche risk, no whumpfing, quite steep open slope, triggered behind me as I took a sharp turn, managed to outrun it, no one was injured.

reports.title: Here There Be Facets
reports.comment: quick: Skinned over Healy Pass then fought our way downhill through bottomless facets to Pharoah Creek. Fought through abysmal breakable crusts over facets trenching to almost waist deep in places. Eventually picked up an an old skin track on the Pharoah Creek Trail and followed it with less difficulty to Shadow Lake Lodge. Visibility was poor but we assumed a widespread cycle was on in the alpine…

reports.title: Twin Cairns
reports.comment: quick: Enjoyed a storm skiing day at Twin Cairns.  Skied on north facing slopes.  Very windy.  10 cm new snow overnight.  Crust was unsupportive in places on the way up, unfortunate as with the wind blowing so hard we needed a new skin track each run.  Skiing down was fine as I stayed on top of the crust.  Heard two large avalanches during the day, with the wind and limited visibility I couldn't t…

reports.title: Goats Eye Study Plot
reports.comment: snowpack: ~45 cm slab of cohesive snow over very weak facets is the main concern in the snowpack. This will likely remain a problem for quite a while.

reports.title: Low angle day at Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Reasonable travel in a good skin track up Healy Creek, although any deviation away from the track saw 50cm ski penetration in walk mode. Evidence of some size 2 natural slides on the Monarch Ramparts ridge with some fresh powder sitting on top. No signs of instabilities though, and some nice turns in the deep powder!

reports.title: Healy Pass Tour
reports.comment: quick: Skied up Healy Creek to Healy Pass today on the trail with 10cm of new snow. Didn't leave the trail but there were plenty of signs of recent natural avalanche activity on low angle slopes in the area. Healy Pass Peak East face slid recently as pictured.

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: snowpack: Approx 30cm of fresh snow on the surface. Facets at 80cm depth which failed after 5 hits from the shoulder.

reports.title: Skier Accidental Howard Douglas Creek
reports.comment: avalanche: Second skier skied to their left to get off of moving snow while the first skier was well down the slope and kept skiing to avoid being caught. A large slab propagated to the right along ridgecrest down into Howard Douglas Creek.

reports.title: Healy to Simpson to SSV
reports.comment:
quick: Went for a walk up Healy creek to the pass and then over to Simpson pass and up to Sunshine slack to ski back in the resort. Ok snow, ski pen was about 15-20cm when breaking trail. 
Dug a pit at the top of Healy pass and found snow depth of about 90cm. 30cm of 4F soft slab sitting on top of 60cm facets/sugar. Did an ECT and had failure on the second elbow tap at the facet/slab interface. Pr…

reports.title: Quartz Ridge avalanche
reports.comment:
avalanche: Reported late in the day on Wednesday, March 26.

Size 3 Natural avalanche. NE aspect. Wide propagation.

reports.title: Sunshine study plot
reports.comment: quick: Sunshine study plot from March 28

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Surprisingly fun day out exploring our new snowpack world in Healy pass. HS at the pass was between 190-200cm. All of the summer trail avalanche paths went big in the last few days but not big enough to reach the summer trail. They were all destructive wet avalanches that looked like they could take out a house. Many large crowns across the ramparts as well but couldn’t get a good photo fro…

reports.title: Fatigue mtn (SSV) + watch those cornices
reports.comment:
quick: Good (and long) day to get to Fatigue, near Citadel. Supportive crust all day in the meadows even though sun was packing a punch and surface snow was moist. Skied the S facing avi path just in front of Citadel. Surface snow was moist but the underlying crust was solid but not too icy either - some slow sluffing but nothing to report aside from really good turns.

Party of 2 looked to have s…

reports.title: Healy Pass Supportive Crust
reports.comment: quick: We skied open slopes in the meadow.  The crust was bomb proof.  Yesterdays trace of snow was just enough turn on.   Good fun on almost zero penetration.  We could see the sides of our skis all day.  Scattered clouds limited solar effects.  There were a few pellet flakes around 1pm.  We finished in the sun.
